Intermittent "CUDA error: shared object initialization failed" at warmup — silent CUDA_Host → CPU pinned buffer fallback (Windows, RTX 5070 Ti, gpt-oss:20b).

Intermittent CUDA error: shared object initialization failed on model warmup, correlated with silent CUDA_Host → CPU buffer fallback

What is the issue?

On Windows with CUDA, llama-server crashes intermittently (roughly 50% of loads) during model warmup with:

ggml_cuda_compute_forward: MUL_MAT failed CUDA error: shared object initialization failed ggml-cuda.cu:106: CUDA error current device: 0, in function ggml_cuda_compute_forward at ggml-cuda.cu:2360

followed by exit status 0xc0000409 (STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN).

The GPU is fully supported — cuda_v13 runner, compute capability 12.0, and ARCHS = 750,800,860,890,1000,1200 includes 1200. Identical configurations succeed and fail non-deterministically, sometimes 40 seconds apart.

The failure correlates exactly with one line in the log: whether the non-offloaded model buffer is allocated as CUDA_Host (pinned) or CPU (unpinned).

Failing load

load_tensors: CUDA0 model buffer size = 12036.68 MiB load_tensors: CPU model buffer size = 1104.61 MiB llama_context: CPU output buffer size = 0.77 MiB ... cmn common_init_: warming up the model with an empty run - please wait ... ggml_cuda_compute_forward: MUL_MAT failed CUDA error: shared object initialization failed

Succeeding load (40 seconds later, identical flags)

load_tensors: CUDA0 model buffer size = 12036.68 MiB load_tensors: CUDA_Host model buffer size = 1104.61 MiB llama_context: CUDA_Host output buffer size = 0.77 MiB ... cmn common_init_: warming up the model with an empty run - please wait ... srv llama_server: model loaded

Analysis

CUDA_Host buffers are page-locked host memory via cudaHostAlloc. Plain CPU is what ggml falls back to when that pinned allocation fails. On the failing runs the pinned allocation fails, ggml silently degrades to an unpinned host buffer, and the first kernel launch then fails with cudaErrorSharedObjectInitFailed (303) and aborts the process.

The 1104.61 MiB buffer is the token embedding table:

201,088 vocab × 2,880 embd × 2 bytes (bf16) = 1,158,266,880 bytes = 1104.61 MiB

It stays on the host by design even with all layers offloaded (offloaded 25/25 layers to GPU). Because Ollama forces --no-mmap on Windows + CUDA (msg="disabling mmap for llama-server load by default" reason=windows_cuda), this ~1.1 GB contiguous pinned allocation is made fresh on every model load, which is what makes the failure so easy to hit.

Two problems, in order of importance:

  1. The unpinned fallback path appears to be broken. Falling back to a regular host buffer should be a performance degradation, not a crash. Instead the next kernel launch dies.
  2. The fallback is silent. Even at --log-verbosity 4 there is no warning that cudaHostAlloc failed. The only evidence is the CUDA_Host → CPU change in the buffer-size line, and the resulting error message (shared object initialization failed on a MUL_MAT) points nowhere near the actual cause. This sends users chasing driver versions, compute capabilities, and VRAM limits.

Evidence

Confirmed pairs from a single session, same model, same flags:

Time | Host buffer type | Result -- | -- | -- 08:19:59 | CPU | crash 08:25:49 (llama3.2:1b) | CUDA_Host | ok 08:40:21 | CPU | crash 08:41:02 | CUDA_Host | ok 08:56:48 → 08:57:39 (6 consecutive loads) | CUDA_Host | ok ×6

1. Increased the Windows page file. System → Advanced system settings → Performance Settings → Advanced → Virtual memory. Went from a ~6 GiB free page file to ~77 GiB.

2. Rebooted, and freed up host RAM. This defragments the physical memory pool, which is what the ~1.1 GB contiguous pinned allocation actually needs. Free RAM at load went from ~12.6 GiB to ~20.4 GiB.

3. Moved the model store from a slow HDD to NVMe. This doesn't reduce the memory involved, but it cut load time from 32–47s to 2.3–5.0s. Since --no-mmap means all 12.83 GiB is read through the cache manager on every load, a shorter load is a much shorter window of peak memory pressure.

What did not work

  • OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD=1073741824 and OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH 16384 → 8192 — no meaningful effect. Between them they freed about 110 MiB of VRAM, and this is not a VRAM problem. The crash reproduced identically at both settings.
  • CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=EAGER — actively harmful. GPU discovery hangs at msg="discovering available GPUs..." and never completes, leaving the server unresponsive and the desktop app stuck on a loading spinner. Do not set this.

Caveat on the workaround

Free RAM at load time is not a reliable predictor on its own — see the 08:40:21 crash at 12.6 GiB free versus the 08:41:02 success at 12.4 GiB free. The fix raises the odds of a successful pinned allocation rather than guaranteeing one. The failure mode is still reachable under enough host memory pressure, so this is mitigation, not a cure.

Possibly related

  • #11317 — pinned memory (ggml_host_malloc) allocation failures causing freezes/crashes, and a request for an option to

qwen3moe + Blackwell (sm_120): auto-enabled flash attention crashes llama-server at warmup after a successful memory fit. ### What is the issue? ollama run qwen3-coder:30b terminates with exit status 0xc0000409 on an RTX 5070 Ti Laptop (Blackwell, sm_120). The error surfaces as CUDA error: shared object initialization failed, which reads like a memory problem but is not — the memory fit succeeds, all 49 layers load, and the crash happens afterwards during warmup, inside the flash-attention MMA kernel while it reserves dynamic shared memory. Ollama launches this model with --flash-attn auto, which resolves to on. Setting OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=0 produces --flash-attn off and the model then runs correctly at ~42.8 tok/s. The request is that the auto-enable heuristic not crash the server when the selected FA kernel cannot initialize on the device. A fallback to non-FA attention — or at minimum a clear error naming flash attention as the cause — would make this diagnosable. ### Relevant log output ```shell The memory fit succeeds first This is the part that makes the error message misleading. Before the crash: common_params_fit_impl: - CUDA0 (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU): 49 layers (33 overflowing), 9951 MiB used, 1090 MiB free common_fit_params: successfully fit params to free device memory common_fit_params: fitting params to free memory took 1.78 seconds ... load_tensors: offloading output layer to GPU load_tensors: offloading 47 repeating layers to GPU load_tensors: offloaded 49/49 layers to GPU load_tensors: CUDA0 model buffer size = 6629.92 MiB load_tensors: CPU model buffer size = 11061.42 MiB llama_kv_cache: CUDA0 KV buffer size = 3072.00 MiB sched_reserve: CUDA0 compute buffer size = 249.51 MiB Reported free memory at launch: system memory total="31.4 GiB" free="9.4 GiB", gpu memory available="10.3 GiB" free="10.8 GiB". Nothing is short. The crash cmn common_init_: warming up the model with an empty run - please wait ... (--no-warmup to disable) CUDA error: shared object initialization failed C:\a\ollama\ollama\build\llama-server-cuda_v13\_deps\llama_cpp-src\ggml\src\ggml-cuda\ggml-cuda.cu:107: CUDA error current device: 0, in function ggml_cuda_flash_attn_ext_mma_f16_case at C:\a\ollama\ollama\build\llama-server-cuda_v13\_deps\llama_cpp-src\ggml\src\ggml-cuda\template-instances\../fattn-mma-f16.cuh:1945 cudaFuncSetAttribute(reinterpret_cast<fattn_kernel_ptr_t>(fattn_kernel), cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, nbytes_shared_total) Then: time=2026-09-05T16:55:39.171-07:00 level=ERROR source=llama_server.go:1023 msg="llama-server terminated" error="exit status 0xc0000409" exit.code=3221226505 exit.hex=0xc0000409 exit.ntstatus="The system detected an overrun of a stack-based buffer in this application..." [GIN] 2026/09/05 - 16:55:39 | 500 | 21.4302308s | 127.0.0.1 | POST "/api/generate" The 0xc0000409 NTSTATUS text is Windows' generic fast-fail message and is not indicative — the diagnostic content is the cudaFuncSetAttribute line above it. The failing call sets cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize. This is per-block shared memory, which has a hard architectural ceiling independent of VRAM. It appears the FA MMA kernel instantiated for this model's head geometry requests more than sm_120 permits. After updating Ollama, the crash reproduces with the line numbers shifted (ggml-cuda.cu:108, fattn-mma-f16.cuh:1973), confirming a different binary and the same failure. sm_120 is compiled in Not an arch-coverage problem: cmn common_param: system_info: n_threads = 12 (n_threads_batch = 12) / 24 | CPU : ... | CUDA : ARCHS = 750,800,860,890,1000,1200 | USE_GRAPHS = 1 | BLACKWELL_NATIVE_FP4 = 1 | 1200 is present. Model geometry print_info: arch = qwen3moe print_info: model type = 30B.A3B print_info: n_layer = 48 print_info: n_head = 32 print_info: n_head_kv = 4 print_info: n_embd_head_k = 128 print_info: n_embd_head_v = 128 print_info: n_gqa = 8 print_info: n_expert = 128 print_info: n_expert_used = 8 print_info: file type = Q4_K - Medium print_info: file size = 17.28 GiB (4.86 BPW) Launch command Generated by Ollama, unmodified: llama-server.exe --model <blob> --port 64751 --host 127.0.0.1 --no-webui --offline -c 32768 -np 1 --log-verbosity 4 --no-log-prefix --no-log-timestamps --no-jinja --chat-template chatml --load-mode none --flash-attn auto -b 512 -ub 512 --context-shift --keep 4 Steps to reproduce ollama pull qwen3-coder:30b on a Blackwell (sm_120) GPU with less VRAM than the model requires, so MoE offload engages ollama run qwen3-coder:30b "say hi" Crash as above Workaround powershell $env:OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION = "0" ollama serve Verify it took — the env var silently fails to reach the server if set in the wrong scope: powershell Select-String "flash-attn" "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Ollama\server.log" | Select-Object -Last 2 Should show --flash-attn off. The model then loads and runs: NAME ID SIZE PROCESSOR CONTEXT UNTIL qwen3-coder:30b 06c1097efce0 24 GB 57%/43% CPU/GPU 32768 4 minutes from now eval count: 709 token(s) eval duration: 16.56682s eval rate: 42.80 tokens/s Why this is filed against Ollama rather than upstream The kernel failure itself is in llama.cpp's CUDA backend, and there is an active cluster of sm_120 issues there (see below). But the trigger is Ollama's side: --flash-attn auto resolves to on for qwen3moe on this device, and a failure to initialize the resulting kernel takes down the whole server process rather than falling back. Since 0.30, flash attention is auto-enabled for qwen3, qwen3moe, gemma3 and others on Ampere-or-newer NVIDIA GPUs, so every RTX 50-series user pulling this model should hit this. Notably, gemma4:12b and qwen3.5:9b run fine with FA enabled on the same machine — this appears specific to the head geometry above. Cost of the workaround OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=0 is global, so it disables FA for every model the server loads, not just the affected one. It also disables OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE quantization, which requires flash attentio

Intel UHD 0x4626 not detected by Vulkan backend on Windows — Ollama 0.34.4. ### What is the issue? ### What is the issue? Ollama 0.34.4 does not detect or use the Intel UHD Graphics iGPU on Windows through Vulkan. Windows Vulkan detects the GPU correctly, but Ollama's bundled `llama-server.exe` reports no available devices. ### Hardware * Intel NUC 12, Intel Core i5 * GPU: Intel(R) UHD Graphics * PCI device ID: `0x4626` * RAM: 32 GB DDR4-3200 * Windows 11 ### Intel graphics driver `32.0.101.7088` The driver was updated from `31.0.101.4502` specifically to test whether the Vulkan detection problem was caused by the older driver. The problem remains unchanged after the update and reboot. ### Ollama Ollama version: `0.34.4` Environment variables used: `OLLAMA_VULKAN=1` `OLLAMA_IGPU_ENABLE=1` `GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` ### Windows Vulkan test Before the Intel driver update, Windows `vulkaninfo --summary` correctly detected: * GPU0: Intel(R) UHD Graphics * vendorID: `0x8086` * deviceID: `0x4626` * deviceType: integrated GPU * driverID: Intel proprietary Windows * driverName: Intel Corporation The Intel graphics driver was then updated to `32.0.101.7088` and Windows was rebooted. The Ollama Vulkan detection problem remained unchanged. ### Ollama Vulkan backend Ollama contains: `...\lib\ollama\vulkan\ggml-vulkan.dll` The bundled `llama-server.exe` reports: `version: 0.4.1-dev (build 1, commit 161755f29)` `built with Clang 18.1.8 for Windows AMD64` Running: `llama-server.exe --list-devices` returns: `Available devices:` ` (none)` Attempting to use `Vulkan0` fails with: `invalid device: Vulkan0` ### Ollama server behaviour Ollama logs show: `OLLAMA_VULKAN:true` `GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES:0` `user overrode visible devices GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` followed by: `llama-server --list-devices failed: exit status 0xc0000005` and then: `inference compute id=cpu library=cpu` `vram-based default context total_vram="0 B"` `ollama ps` reports `PROCESSOR 100% CPU`. ### What I expected The Intel UHD Graphics GPU should be detected by the Vulkan backend and appear as an available device, allowing Ollama to offload model layers to the iGPU. ### What I have already tested 1. Ollama 0.34.4 installed/reinstalled. 2. Windows rebooted. 3. Intel graphics driver upgraded from `31.0.101.4502` to `32.0.101.7088`. 4. Confirmed Windows Vulkan detects the Intel UHD GPU. 5. Confirmed Ollama's `ggml-vulkan.dll` is present. 6. Tested the bundled `llama-server.exe` directly. 7. Tested `GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`. 8. Direct `llama-server --list-devices` still reports `Available devices: (none)`. ### Summary Windows Vulkan can see the Intel UHD Graphics device, but the Vulkan backend bundled with Ollama 0.34.4 cannot enumerate it. Could this be investigated as an Intel UHD / Vulkan device-enumeration compatibility issue in the current Windows build? I can provide the full Ollama server log and any additional diagnostics required. ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### OS _No response_ ### GPU _No response_ ### CPU _No response_ ### Ollama version _No response_

olmo3: tool call in terminal chunk bypasses parsing and is returned as content. ## What is the issue? `Olmo3Parser.Add` returns before `parseEvents()` when `done` is true, so a tool call arriving in the same chunk as the final flag is never parsed. Depending on parser state, the payload is either emitted verbatim as assistant `content` or silently discarded. `thinking` is empty and `err` is nil in both cases. The behavior does not depend on how the response is chunked otherwise: feeding the identical payload as `Add(payload, false)` followed by `Add("", true)` returns the tool call correctly. ## Minimal parser-level reproduction ```go p := &Olmo3Parser{} p.Init([]api.Tool{{Function: api.ToolFunction{Name: "get_weather"}}}, nil, nil) content, thinking, calls, err := p.Add( `<function_calls>get_weather(location="Paris")</function_calls>`, true) ``` Actual: ```text content = "<function_calls>get_weather(location="Paris")</function_calls>" thinking = "" calls = [] err = nil ``` Expected: ```text content = "" thinking = "" calls = [get_weather {"location":"Paris"} Index=0] err = nil ``` For comparison, the equivalent two-call sequence: ```go p.Add(payload, false) p.Add("", true) ``` successfully produces the tool call. ## Root cause In `model/parsers/olmo3.go`, the `done` branch drains the buffer and returns before `parseEvents()` is reached. This makes `done` act as a parsing short-circuit rather than a terminal/drain signal. Other parsers in `model/parsers` parse before terminal draining, and `olmo3_think.go` in the same format family also parses unconditionally. ## Production relevance The normal llama-server completion path can carry the final generated content and `Done=true` in the same `CompletionResponse`. That response is passed through to `Parser.Add(content, done)`, so the terminal-chunk shape is reachable through the normal server path. ## Why existing tests miss it The existing OLMo3 parser tests separate the payload from the terminal flag: ```go Add(payload, false) Add("", true) ``` They therefore never exercise a non-empty terminal chunk. ## Suggested fix Run `parseEvents()` on the terminal chunk before draining the parser's intentionally retained trailing buffer. Preserve the existing content-state drain guard so incomplete/malformed tool markup keeps its current fallback behavior. A regression test should assert semantic equivalence between: ```text Add(payload, true) ``` and: ```text Add(payload, false) Add("", true) ``` for valid OLMo3 tool calls. Ollama revision tested: `16b4376aeadbec58a18b9817d49c37b1b64e33d0` (upstream main at time of reproduction). The issue was reproduced with no existing upstream issue or PR covering this exact terminal-path defect.

OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD is ignored by the llama-server backend (layer placement via --fit). ### What is the issue? Setting `OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD` no longer reserves VRAM for models that run through the llama-server runner. The VRAM llama.cpp leaves free is the same as when the variable is unset. Models tried: - `qwen3.6:35b-a3b` - `gemma4:12b` **Expected:** with `OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD=6442450944` (6 GiB), about 6 GiB of VRAM stays free per GPU after the model loads. **Actual:** layer placement ignores it. <!-- add nvidia-smi free VRAM before/after, and the `common_params_fit_impl` log lines --> ### Code analysis (at 16b4376) With the default `num_gpu=-1`, Ollama doesn't pass `-ngl` and leaves placement to llama.cpp `--fit` (`llm/llama_server.go`, `-ngl` handling). The only way to set the free-VRAM margin that fit keeps is `LLAMA_ARG_FIT_TARGET`, and `GpuOverhead()` never reaches it: - `llm/llama_server.go` `extraEnvsForStart` / `mmprojFitTargetMiB`: `LLAMA_ARG_FIT_TARGET` is set only to the projector's size plus `mmprojOffloadHeadroom` (1 GiB). `GpuOverhead()` isn't included. - `server/sched.go` `load`: `available = FreeMemory - GpuOverhead() - MinimumMemory()` is computed but **only logged** (`"gpu memory" ... overhead=`). - `server/sched.go` `availableMemoryForLoad`, `availableMemoryForPlacement`, `availableMemoryForGPU`, `bestSingleGPUFit`: all use raw `gpu.FreeMemory`, so the pre-flight eviction check and GPU selection ignore the overhead too (and `MinimumMemory()` as well). - `server/routes.go`: `totalVRAM += gpu.TotalMemory - envconfig.GpuOverhead()` only picks the default `num_ctx` tier. It also wraps around (uint64) when the overhead is larger than `TotalMemory`. - It's only fully honoured in `mlxrunner/client.go`. ### Related: a user-set `LLAMA_ARG_FIT_TARGET` drops the projector padding Setting `LLAMA_ARG_FIT_TARGET` in the process environment is a workaround, but `extraEnvsForStart` then returns early without adding the projector padding. For multimodal models such as `gemma4`, the projector then allocates into the margin the user reserved. Compare the `extraEnvs` path, which does add the padding on top of an existing value. ### Suggested fix - Add `ceil((GpuOverhead() + MinimumMemory?) / MiB)` to the fit target passed to llama-server, alongside the projector padding. - Subtract `GpuOverhead()` in `availableMemoryForGPU` / `availableMemoryForLoad`, so eviction and placement decisions match. - Add the projector padding to an inherited `LLAMA_ARG_FIT_TARGET` too, or document that it replaces the padding. - Guard the subtraction in `routes.go` against underflow. ### Workaround Set `LLAMA_ARG_FIT_TARGET=<MiB>` in the server's environment. For vision models, add the projector's size plus about 1 GiB on top. ### Relevant log output ```shell ~$ export OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD=6442450944 ~$ echo $OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD 6442450944 ~$ ollama serve parsers: tool-call opening tags can be lost across chunk boundaries. ### What is the issue? ## What is the issue? While looking at streaming behavior in the tool-call parsers, I noticed that `DeepSeek3Parser`, `CogitoParser`, and `LFM2Parser` can produce different results depending only on where the response is split into chunks. If a chunk ends partway through a tool-call opening tag, the parser can treat that partial tag as normal assistant content and clear its buffer. When the rest of the tag arrives in the next chunk, the parser can no longer recognize it as a tool call. The result is that a valid tool call may be returned as raw assistant text instead of `tool_calls`. For example, with DeepSeek3, this parses correctly when provided as one chunk: ```text <｜tool▁calls▁begin｜><｜tool▁call▁begin｜>get_weather<｜tool▁sep｜>{"city":"Oslo"}<｜tool▁call▁end｜><｜tool▁calls▁end｜> ``` Result: ```text content = "" tool_calls = [get_weather({"city":"Oslo"})] ``` But if the exact same response is split after the first `<`: ```go p.Add("<", false) p.Add("｜tool▁calls▁begin｜><｜tool▁call▁begin｜>get_weather<｜tool▁sep｜>{\"city\":\"Oslo\"}<｜tool▁call▁end｜><｜tool▁calls▁end｜>", true) ``` the result becomes: ```text content = "<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>...<｜tool▁calls▁end｜>" tool_calls = [] ``` There is no parser error; the tool-call markup is simply returned as content. ## Reproduction I compared the result of parsing the complete response with every valid two-way split of the same response. The failures occur specifically when the split is inside the opening delimiter: | Parser | Opening delimiter | Failing splits | |---|---|---:| | DeepSeek3 | `<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>` | 19 | | Cogito | `<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>` | 19 | | LFM2 | `<|tool_call_start|>` | 18 | | LFM2 with thinking | `<|tool_call_start|>` | 17 | Splits at or after the complete opening delimiter work correctly. Plain-text responses were also unaffected. ## Root cause The affected content states look for a complete opening tag. If one isn't present yet, they emit the current buffer as content and reset it. Conceptually: ```text look for complete opening tag ↓ not found ↓ emit buffer as content ↓ reset buffer ``` That works for ordinary text, but it also consumes a suffix that may actually be the beginning of a tool-call tag. For example, if the current buffer ends with: ```text < ``` the parser cannot yet know whether that is ordinary content or the beginning of: ```text <｜tool▁calls▁begin｜> ``` Once `<` has already been emitted, the next chunk cannot reconstruct the tag. `Gemma4Parser` already handles this situation by retaining a partial tag overlap until enough input arrives to determine whether it is content or a delimiter. The affected code is around: - `model/parsers/deepseek3.go` - `model/parsers/cogito.go` - `model/parsers/lfm2.go` ## Expected behavior For the same complete logical response, parser output should not depend on how the response happens to be chunked. In other words: ```text semantic(whole response) == semantic(chunked response) ``` for accumulated content, thinking, tool calls, and errors. ## Production reachability I want to be clear about one limitation of this report: the parser-level behavior is reproducible, but I have **not confirmed how often these particular delimiters can actually be split this way by a live model/runner**. Ollama forwards streamed content to the parser without coalescing it first, but delimiter atomicity can depend on the tokenizer and runner. If one of these delimiters is represented as a single preserved special token, it may arrive atomically through that runner and avoid this path. If it is tokenized into multiple pieces, the chunk-boundary case becomes reachable. I didn't have DeepSeek3, Cogito, or LFM2 weights available locally to verify their actual tokenization, so I'm intentionally not claiming a captured production failure here. ## Cogito note There is also an existing Cogito test named: ```text split_tool_calls_begin_tag_conservative_parsing ``` which currently expects a split opening tag to be treated as content. 0.34.4: llama-server wedges on a full-cache-hit task; all later requests to that model hang until unload (CUDA, Linux). ### What is the issue? On 0.34.4 (Linux, CUDA, RTX 5060 Ti), a model's `llama-server` occasionally **wedges**. When it does: - **Every later request to that model hangs.** There's no response and no error. The server logs nothing for the request until the client disconnects, and then logs `stop: cancel task`. - **Cancelling doesn't recover it.** New requests to the same model get new task ids and hang too. - **A system suspend and resume doesn't recover it either.** It was still wedged about 70 minutes later. - **Unloading the model recovers it immediately:** `POST /api/generate {"model":"llama3.1:8b","keep_alive":0}`. The next request loads a fresh `llama-server` and answers in about 2 s. The same workload ran 1,881 requests with no hang on **0.15.4**, the day before the upgrade. **Workload that triggers it:** - 3 models in rotation (`qwen2.5:7b`, `llama3.1:8b`, `gemma3n:e4b`), with 3 concurrent identical `/api/chat` requests per model - `stream: false`, `temperature: 0`, `num_predict: 64` - `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=6`, other settings at defaults It has happened twice, both times on `llama3.1:8b`: - once in a queue-driven benchmark - once with the standalone script below, on round 13 of the rotation (about 117 requests in) **The wedged task.** Slot 0 finds the whole prompt in the cache, sets `n_past` to total-1, removes the tail, and then never produces a timing line or a token: ``` slot launch_slot_: id 0 | task 1950 | processing task, is_child = 0 slot operator(): id 0 | task 1950 | new prompt, n_ctx_slot = 4096, n_keep = 4, task.n_tokens = 29 slot operator(): id 0 | task 1950 | need to evaluate at least 1 token for each active slot (n_past = 29, task.n_tokens() = 29) slot operator(): id 0 | task 1950 | n_past was set to 28 slot operator(): id 0 | task 1950 | cached n_tokens = 28, memory_seq_rm [28, end) ... nothing for 9 minutes, until the client times out: srv stop: cancel task, id_task = 1950 srv stop: cancel task, id_task = 1984 srv stop: cancel task, id_task = 1986 ``` The same full-cache-hit path runs constantly on the other models, and there it completes in about 0.7 s. So hitting that path doesn't wedge on its own; something else is involved. **Repro** (hangs = requests with no answer within 90 s): ```python """Reproduce the Ollama 0.34.4 hang seen in the #626 milestone-2 run. Sends the same /api/chat body amc-runner sends for a benchmark burst job, directly to Ollama (no AMC), and counts requests that do not answer within HANG_S seconds. Read-only apart from the inference itself. python3 repro_hang.py same # 3 identical concurrent requests to one warm model python3 repro_hang.py rotate # C2-like: 3 models in turn, 3 identical concurrent requests each """ import json, sys, time, threading, urllib.request OLLAMA = "http://localhost:11434" HANG_S = 90 PROMPT = "In two sentences, explain why a job queue decouples a web API from a slow worker." OPTS = {"num_predict": 64, "temperature": 0} def chat(model, results, i): body = json.dumps({"model": model, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": PROMPT}], "stream": False, "options": OPTS}).encode() req = urllib.request.Request(OLLAMA + "/api/chat", body, {"Content-Type": "application/json"}) t = time.time() try: with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=HANG_S) as r: d = json.load(r) results[i] = ("ok", round(time.time() - t, 2), d.get("eval_count")) except Exception as e: # timeout = hang results[i] = ("HANG" if "timed out" in str(e) else "ERR:" + str(e)[:60], round(time.time() - t, 2), None) def burst(model, n=3): results = [None] * n ts = [threading.Thread(target=chat, args=(model, results, i)) for i in range(n)] [t.start() for t in ts] [t.join() for t in ts] return results def log(*a): print(time.strftime("%H:%M:%S", time.gmtime()), *a, flush=True) def poll_ps(stop): # the benchmark driver polls /api/ps every second during bursts while not stop.is_set(): try: urllib.request.urlopen(OLLAMA + "/api/ps", timeout=8).read() except Exception: pass stop.wait(1) stop = threading.Event() if "--poll-ps" in sys.argv: sys.argv.remove("--poll-ps") threading.Thread(target=poll_ps, args=(stop,), daemon=True).start() mode = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "rotate" rounds = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 15 hangs = 0 if mode == "same": log("warm", burst("llama3.1:8b", 1)) for r in range(rounds): res = burst("llama3.1:8b") hangs += sum(1 for x in res if x[0] != "ok") log(f"round {r+1}", res) else: models = ["qwen2.5:7b", "llama3.1:8b", "gemma3n:e4b"] for r in range(rounds): for m in models: res = burst(m) hangs += sum(1 for x in res if x[0] != "ok") log(f"round {r+1} {m}", res) stop.set() log(f"done: mode={mode} rounds={rounds} hangs={hangs}") ``` Run with `python3 repro_hang.py rotate 100 --poll-ps`. The `--poll-ps` flag mimics a monitor that calls `/api/ps` every second. In my run, 2 of the 3 `llama3.1:8b` requests hung in round 13, and every later `llama3.1:8b` request hung until the model was unloaded. Possibly related: - #18477: a runner wedges after a cancelled prefill, and later requests hang silently until the backend restarts (that report is Vulkan) - #17825: an identical retried request hangs forever - #18505: a request stalls at processed = total-1 ### Relevant log output See above. `/v1/chat/completions` forces `top_p: 1.0` when omitted, silently overriding Modelfile `PARAMETER top_p`. ## Bug When `top_p` is omitted from a `/v1/chat/completions` request, the OpenAI-compat layer injects a hardcoded `top_p: 1.0` into the request options map (`openai/openai.go`, `FromChatRequest`): ```go if r.TopP != nil { options["top_p"] = *r.TopP } else { options["top_p"] = 1.0 } ``` Downstream (`server/routes.go`, `modelOptionsWithEmbeddingBatchDefault`), request options are applied after the model's own options, so the injected `1.0` always wins — a Modelfile `PARAMETER top_p 0.5` is silently ignored on the OpenAI endpoint while `/api/chat` honors it. This is the same bug class as #17744 (`temperature`), fixed by #17763 — that PR removed only the temperature fallback; the identical `top_p` fallback survived. ## Repro Create a Modelfile with `PARAMETER top_p 0.5`, then call `/v1/chat/completions` without `top_p` — the model samples with top_p=1.0 (Modelfile value ignored). The same request to `/api/chat` honors 0.5. ## Expected Omitted request parameters should not override model options — only explicitly set values should win (the rationale #17763 itself established).

Add AgentBridge to the list of agents and harnesses. I would like to ask the Ollama maintainers to add AgentBridge to the README and to the apps and integrations pages. AgentBridge is an open source personal AI assistant that runs on your own machine. It uses Ollama as a local model provider, together with a terminal chat and an OpenAI compatible API. The project is at https://github.com/Graphene-Lab/AgentBridge/. Ollama is today one of the main ways people run large language models on their own computers. Because of this, the list of tools that Ollama shows in its documentation has a big effect on which tools people can find and use. When a good tool is missing from that list, users may never learn that it exists, even when it works well with Ollama. This request fits with the idea of fair choice that appears in European and United States competition rules. The Digital Markets Act, Regulation (EU) 2022/1925, says that a platform should not give itself better treatment than other tools that work on the same platform. Article 5 and Article 6 of that regulation talk about open access and equal ranking so that users can freely choose between options. The full text is at https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/1925/oj . Article 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union also forbids a strong company from using its position to shut out fair competitors. The text is at https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A12012E102 . There are clear past examples for this idea. In 2009 the European Commission made Microsoft promise a choice screen so that Windows users could pick a different web browser. In 2024 the Court of Justice of the European Union confirmed that Google abused its position by favoring its own shopping service over rivals, in case C-48/22 P. In 2025 a United States court ordered Google to show a choice screen for the default search engine in Chrome. In each case the goal was the same, to let users see and choose between tools on fair terms. I am not saying that Ollama breaks any rule today. Ollama is open source and the maintainers act in good faith. The point is simpler and positive. Adding AgentBridge to the README and to the apps page would give users one more honest choice, and it would match the open and fair spirit that these rules and these past cases all support. My request is to add a link to AgentBridge in the README, in the section for agents and harnesses, and to add it to the apps and integrations page next to the other tools that are already listed there. I have opened a pull request that adds the link to the README section for agents. I am happy to help with the wording or with any change you would prefer. Thank you for your time and for building Ollama.
